findings.title: Do not cache devices whose admission was rejected
findings.body: Propagating the store error does not make the device limit effective because tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, its cache entry remains for 29 minutes. The next request with the same device ID hits that entry, returns nil, and successfully authenticates anonymously despite the limit. Only cache successful admissions, and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

findings.title: Make the device-count check and admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or other serialization. If two new devices arrive when one slot remains, both can observe a count below deviceLimit and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Once inserted, both devices qualify for updates even while over the limit. Enforce the count check and admission atomically using database-level concurrency control, and cover concurrent admissions in tests.
